records.region: Southern Baffin Island, Nunavut, Canada; inland pond and wetland corridor approaching the Foxe Basin coast south of the large northern river mouth.
records.material_pending_reason: Readable independent imagery establishes the geographic setting but does not establish all selected pond, wetland and terminal-branch connections. The independent lake-survey map is regional context rather than a full-route depiction.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No name is attached to the selected feature. Nettilling Lake, Amadjuak River and Koukdjuak River are regional context or initially considered leads, not selected-feature identities.
records.completion_scope: Bounded source pass completed; no representative name or full selected-route correspondence claimed.
records.supported_name_scope: No name is attached to the selected feature. Nettilling Lake, Amadjuak River and Koukdjuak River are regional context or initially considered leads, not selected-feature identities.

scope_limits: No independently inspected source attaches a hydronym to FID 2548.
The opening, upper pond connections, intermediate wetland joins and final branch-to-outlet connection are not all established at ordinary corridor scale.
The actual receiving-shore setting is identified, but this does not resolve the selected last-channel connection among adjacent drainage branches.
The source imagery is a mosaic of unspecified local acquisition dates. It supplies geographic observations, not proof of present-day flow or seasonality.
The historical source-limit ledger remains incomplete. Its missing entries do not constitute clearance of potentially related publications.
No exact bank, vertex or current-flow proof was required; remaining gaps concern the selected sequence of waterbody and channel connections.

records.region: Honduras and El Salvador border region
records.material_pending_reason: Missing eastern upper connection within FID10644, late FID10645 and both joins of FID10646, lower FID10647 and the actual western terminal FID10648. Names at the mapped intervals do not establish these through-links.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Selected south-Honduras/El Salvador border-region drainage with separately named Honduran upper reaches. Adjacent mapped tributaries are not substituted for the selection. The selected terminal is not treated as the generic Gulf of Fonseca outlet merely because the basin drains there.
records.completion_scope: All five selected mainstem fragments are recorded. The Cancire, Quebrada Honda and Palagua upper corridor and mapped middle Goascorán interval are supported. The eastern connector, late middle/lower fragments and western actual terminal remain incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: Bounded mapped receiving-reach candidate only; the full selected system is not completed. Distinct Cancire, Quebrada Honda and Palagua upper reach names remain separately scoped.

scope_limits: Names have bounded directly read reach scopes; no claim that every modeled mainstem part shares one name.
Historical maps establish ordinary corridor correspondence, not present banks, discharge or management operations.
No exact official naming boundary, registry identity or Korean rendering is established.
The source-material gap, not exact-bank/current-operation precision, is why the result remains incomplete.

scope_limits: The opening-to-upper-lake connection and extended southern U-shaped transfer are real source-correspondence gaps, not demands for exact banks, current discharge or vertex matching.

Satellite/aerial mosaic scene dates are unestablished, and the two acquisitions do not prove present flow or water levels.

records.region: Eastern Victoria Island, Nunavut; upper Ekalluk River and locally named Ekalluk Lake, with a selected eastern continuation toward Albert Edward Bay.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected eastward transfer from the broad Ekalluk Lake area and lower coastal continuation are not established. The two independent originals instead support the named upper Ekalluk corridor continuing south through the Ferguson Lake system to Wellington Bay. A nearby coastal name cannot repair the missing eastern through-link.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Upper selected river and its entry into the broad middle lake. Not a representative identity for the complete selected eastward-to-coast route.
records.completion_scope: Bounded source research and factual finding prepared for all 25 selected parts. Named upper components are supported; complete selected geographic correspondence and representative identity are not. This is one source-material-pending state, not a completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: Ekalluk River is printed along the selected upper reach. Ekalluk Lake is the map’s explicitly local name for the broad middle waterbody. Albert Edward Bay is the receiving coastal setting; each retains its own geographic role.

scope_limits: The entire selected line may combine an upper Ekalluk component with a distinct eastern drainage; the missing through-links prevent a whole-system identity. No correction to the selected geometry is proposed.
The middle lake’s historical local map name and the thesis’s unnamed-lake description are preserved without claiming current official status.
The selected lower route’s precise relationship to Char/Fish Trap drainage remains unresolved. Jayco is a separate depicted outlet, so its name is not assigned.
No present discharge, seasonal passability, bank-exact alignment, hydraulic operation, formal naming boundary or definitive ultimate source is asserted.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
